sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:-
"....to issue a writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of nd Mandamus declaring the action of the 2 respondent in trying to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the petitioners land i.e. Plots bearing No.9 and 10 situated in S.No.484/4, Sivajyothi Nagar, Tirupati within the limits of Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) purportedly for road-widening without any prior A. 1 notice and despite objections raised by the petitioners by letter dated 30.07.2024 as illegal, arbitrary, contrary to principles of natural justice, provisions of the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1994 besides being violative of Articles 14, 21 and 300(A) of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents not to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the petitioners land i.e.
Plots bearing No.9 and 10 situated in S.No.484/4, Sivajyothi Nagar, Tirupati ..."
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that the petitioners No.1 and 2 purchased Plot Nos.9 and 10 situated in S.No.484/4, Sivajyothi Nagar, Tirupati from the lawful owners under registered deeds and has been in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the same.
The petitioners have been paying property tax regularly without any default.

3. While so, the respondent No.2 has proposed to widen the road already existed passing through the plots of petitioners from 10 feet to 40 feet in the name of Master Plan road from Raghavendra Nagar to Akkarampalle Road.
In that view, the respondent No.2 requested the petitioners and other plot owners to surrender their land and for which an adequate compensation would be paid to them.
Accepting the same, the petitioner surrendered 15 feet of their land in their plots.
On such surrender the respondents demolished RCC houses which are existed in the plot Nos.9 and 10.
Thereafter, the petitioners made several representations to grant of compensation and damages.

But till date, there is no response from the respondent No.2.
4.

Like that of the matter, one C.Lakshmi Jyoshna, who is owner of plot No.7 filed W.P.No.17719 of 2023 before this Court, in which, an interim order was also granted in her favour directing the respondents not to demolish the house of said Jyoshna.
It is stated that plot No.7 is situated opposite to plot Nos.9 and 10 of petitioners.
Due to subsistence of interim orders of this Court, the respondent No.2 could not acquire the 15 feet of land in plot No.7.

However, with a view to accomplish the formation of 40 feet master plan road, the respondent No.2 is now proposing to acquire another 15 feet of land in plot Nos.9 and 10 which belongs to petitioners herein.
The respondent authorities are threatened the petitioners that their lands would be acquired.

Despite the same, the petitioners submitted a representation dated 30.07.2024 to the respondent No.2,
requesting not to encroach high-handedly and illegally over the subject property without following the due process of law and to provide compensation for the acquisition of 15 feet of land already surrendered in the subject property.
However, the respondent No.2 did not consider the same so far.
Challenging which, the present writ petition is filed.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
6.

At the time of hearing, learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration and Urban Development and Mr.Kalava Suresh, learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.2-Tirupati Municipal Corporation submitted that if at all the respondents intend to acquire the petitioners'
land, they will follow the due process of law.

sentences.text: Recording the submission made by the learned counsel for the respondents, instead of going into the merits of the case, the writ petition is disposed of by directing respondent No.2-The Commissioner, Tirupati Municipal Corporation to pass appropriate orders on the representation dated 30.07.2024 submitted by the petitioners, within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order in accordance with law.

However, the respondent authorities are directed not to interfere with the petitioners' property i.e. Plot Nos.9 and 10 situated in S.No.484/4,
Sivajyothi Nagar, Tirupati without following due process of law.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall also stand closed.
